summary: Philips reached an agreement with the Department of Justice to pay 288 million euros (about $322 million) to settle criminal and civil investigations related to its recall of millions of sleep and respiratory devices, the company disclosed Tuesday. Philips began the recall of more than 15 million devices in 2021 after finding soundproofing foam could break down and be inhaled by users. The recall included continuous positive airway pressure and bilevel positive airway pressure machines, as well as ventilators. The settlement is separate from a consent decree the Food and Drug Administration struck with Philips in 2024, which has barred the sale of certain respiratory devices in the U.S. until Philips meets requirements set out by the agency.
title: Philips settles with DOJ over recalled CPAP machines

summary: Physicians, artificial intelligence developers and healthcare organizations that deploy clinical AI tools all bear distinct responsibilities for ensuring the tools do not cause patient harm, the American Medical Association said in an issue brief released last week. While physicians remain responsible for exercising their clinical judgment, developers are accountable for designing safe AI tools, the physician advocacy group said. At the same time, deployers are responsible for selecting the right tool for clinical scenarios, providing physicians' training and monitoring the AI's performance. Currently, physicians are being asked to become a safety net to protect against clinical AI failures that could harm patients, but that means they may be held accountable for risks that they cannot control and, "in some cases, may not even be able to identify," Jennifer Goldsack, head of the AMA Center on Digital Health and AI, said in an interview.
title: AI vendors, health systems join physicians in liability for clinical AI: AMA

summary: Bracco is investing $230 million to construct its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media, the company said last week. Bracco will build the facility in Sanford, North Carolina. The company expects to create 200 jobs and could receive a $2.9 million grant over 12 years. Adding U.S. production capacity could enhance the resilience of the supply chain, which failed to meet demand for iodinated contrast media during a pandemic-related lockdown in 2022.
title: Bracco invests $230M to build US plant for injectable contrast media

summary: Abbott has started a pivotal clinical trial of its investigational Cephea mitral valve system, the company said Thursday. The device, which Abbott acquired in its 2019 takeover of Cephea Valve Technologies, replaces the diseased mitral valve to restore normal blood flow through the heart. Cephea performs the same function as Abbott’s Tendyne but is delivered through a vein in the leg, rather than via a small incision in the chest.
title: Abbott starts pivotal trial for mitral valve replacement device
